visual_thesis: Lower adjusted AI use in health occupations differs by task, with medical care an exception; adoption is not measured productivity.
mechanism_metaphor: One large irregular folded task specimen occupies the left two thirds. Four meaningful exposed layers are labeled Ideas, Administration, Summaries and Data analysis, grouped beneath General tasks and Lower adjusted use. At upper right a magnified smaller part of the same specimen isolates Medical care with Higher adjusted use. A small Survey evidence packet at lower right points with one arrow to the physical task-comparison specimen, representing analysis of survey observations rather than a causal claim that occupations change use. Never draw bars, percentages, slopes, ticks or measured distances; layer size is illustrative and not proportional to prevalence. A detached lower-right qualifier reads Use is not productivity and a lower-left scope note reads Combined roles; survey limits. Distinguish the exception through location, material and exact words, not color alone. The drawing should reveal the four task categories and the exceptional clinical task at 320px without implying which specific job roles drive the gap.
story_anchors: Adjusted survey comparisons show lower use for general-purpose tasks in health occupations and higher medical-care use as the exception.
Occupational categories combine roles and survey limitations prevent claims about objective productivity or causal effects.
